## Purpose

This SOP describes the laboratory procedures for drying, grinding, and
preparing plant tissue samples for subsequent elemental, isotopic, or
nutrient analysis. Proper sample preparation is essential for obtaining
representative, reproducible analytical results. The procedures follow
standard methods for plant analysis [@kalra1998; @mills2004;
@jones2001].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Leaf, stem, root, litter, and other plant tissue
  samples collected from EA Program field sites, prepared for total
  carbon and nitrogen (EA-IRMS), total phosphorus, metal analysis
  (ICP-MS after digestion), or other elemental determinations
- **Does not apply to:** Fresh tissue assays that require unfixed
  material (e.g., chlorophyll extraction from fresh leaves, enzyme
  activity assays); seed or fruit tissue with high oil content
  (requires freeze-drying); soil organic matter (see
  [SOP-L406](SOP-L406-loss-on-ignition.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve drying protocol and grinding method |
| Trained Personnel | Process samples per this SOP                |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |

## Definitions

- **Acid washing (plant tissue):** Cleaning tissue with dilute HCl to remove surface contamination (dust, soil particles, fertilizer residues) before analysis for trace metals or nutrients; may be inappropriate for samples requiring analysis of acid-labile compounds.
- **Air drying:** Drying plant tissue at ambient temperature (typically 20--40 °C) to a stable moisture content; used as a preliminary step before oven drying; preserves enzyme activity and RNA better than direct oven drying.
- **Ball milling:** Size reduction by grinding samples between hardened steel or ceramic balls inside a rotating vessel; the preferred method for producing a homogeneous powder from fibrous plant tissue for EA-IRMS and elemental analysis.
- **Critical tissue concentration:** The minimum concentration of a nutrient required for maximum growth; below this level the plant is deficient; above it, growth is normal or the nutrient may be toxic at very high levels.
- **Lyophilization (freeze drying):** Removal of water from tissue under vacuum after rapid freezing; preserves cell structure, volatile compounds, and biological activity better than oven drying; required for enzyme, RNA, and some metabolite analyses.
- **Subsampling:** Drawing a representative small portion from a bulk dried, ground sample for analysis; requires thorough mixing and homogenization of the bulk powder before subsampling to ensure the subsample is representative.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Drying ovens operate at 60--105 °C; burn risk from
  hot trays and glassware. The Wiley mill and ball mill contain
  rapidly moving parts; keep hands, hair, and loose clothing away from
  the grinding chamber.
- **Noise:** The Wiley mill generates noise above 85 dBA. Wear hearing
  protection during operation.
- **Dust:** Grinding produces fine particulate matter. Work in a
  well-ventilated area or use a dust mask, especially when processing
  large batches.
- **Biological:** Field-collected plant tissue may harbor ticks,
  spiders, or allergenic compounds (e.g., poison oak resin). Inspect
  samples before handling; wear gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Hearing protection (Wiley mill operation)
- [ ] Dust mask or N95 respirator (grinding large batches)

### Emergency Procedures

For burns from the oven, cool affected area under running water.
Refer to [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Drying oven                           | Forced-air convection; set to 60 °C (standard) or 105 °C (rapid dry) |
| Wiley mill (Thomas Scientific)        | With 1 mm (20-mesh) screen              |
| Ball mill or mortar and pestle         | For fine grinding (< 250 $\mu$m) for IRMS |
| Analytical balance                    | 0.0001 g readability (for weighing into tin capsules) |
| Desiccator with desiccant             | For cooling dried samples               |

### Consumables

| Item                              | Notes                              |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| Paper bags or aluminum foil trays | For oven drying; labeled with pencil |
| Labeled sample bags (polyethylene or paper) | For storing ground tissue |
| Tin capsules (5 x 9 mm)          | For EA-IRMS analysis               |
| Kimwipes                          | For cleaning mill between samples  |
| 70% ethanol (spray bottle)        | For decontaminating equipment      |


## Procedure

### Sample Receiving and Cleaning

1. Log incoming samples in the laboratory tracking spreadsheet. Verify
   site ID, date, species or tissue type, and collector.
2. If tissue was not rinsed in the field, briefly rinse leaf or stem
   material with deionized water to remove surface soil, dust, and
   epiphytes. Do not soak, as leaching of soluble compounds will occur
   [@kalra1998].
3. Blot excess water with paper towels.
4. For root samples, remove adhering soil by gentle agitation in DI
   water; multiple rinses may be required.

### Drying

1. Place cleaned tissue in labeled paper bags or foil trays. Do not
   overload bags; tissue should be loosely arranged to allow air
   circulation.
2. Dry at 60 °C in the forced-air oven for a minimum of 48 hours, or
   until constant mass is achieved (two consecutive weighings 4 hours
   apart differ by less than 0.1% of sample mass) [@jones2001].
3. For samples intended only for total C and N by combustion (not
   volatile compound analysis), drying at 70 °C is acceptable and
   reduces drying time.

::: {.callout-important}
Do not exceed 70 °C for samples intended for nitrogen analysis, as
volatile nitrogen compounds may be lost at higher temperatures. Do not
exceed 60 °C for samples intended for analysis of volatile organic
compounds, essential oils, or lipids [@kalra1998].
:::

4. Remove dried samples from the oven and cool in a desiccator for at
   least 30 minutes before weighing or grinding.
5. Record the dry mass if gravimetric moisture content is needed.

### Coarse Grinding (Wiley Mill)

1. Inspect the mill: confirm the 1 mm (20-mesh) screen is installed
   and the cutting blades are sharp and properly seated.
2. Turn on the mill and allow it to reach full speed before feeding
   material.
3. Feed dried tissue into the hopper in small amounts, pushing
   material gently with the wooden plunger. Do not force tissue into
   the blades.
4. Collect the ground material passing through the screen in a clean,
   labeled container or bag.
5. Between samples, disassemble the grinding chamber and clean
   thoroughly:
   - Brush all surfaces with a stiff brush to remove residual material
   - Wipe with 70% ethanol
   - Run a small amount of acid-washed quartz sand through the mill
     as a blank grind if cross-contamination of trace metals is a
     concern
   - Allow to dry before the next sample

### Fine Grinding (for IRMS or Homogeneity-Critical Analyses)

For EA-IRMS analysis, the Wiley-milled material (less than 1 mm) must
be further ground to a fine, homogeneous powder (less than 250 $\mu$m):

1. Transfer approximately 1--2 g of coarsely ground tissue to a clean
   ball mill vial with grinding balls.
2. Grind for 2--3 minutes until the material is a uniform fine powder.
3. Alternatively, use an agate mortar and pestle, grinding until no
   gritty texture remains.
4. Transfer the powder to a labeled vial or sample bag.
5. Clean the ball mill vial and balls between samples with 70% ethanol
   and Kimwipes.

### Weighing into Tin Capsules (for EA-IRMS)

1. Using the analytical balance, tare a tin capsule on the balance pan.
2. Weigh 3--5 mg of finely ground tissue into the capsule
   [@brodie2011]. Record the mass to 0.001 mg.
3. Fold the capsule into a tight pellet using forceps, ensuring no
   material escapes.
4. Place the pellet in a labeled well of a microplate or sample tray.
5. Include blanks (empty tin capsules) and reference materials (e.g.,
   acetanilide, USGS-40) in the run sequence per
   [SOP-L414](SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Grind and analyze duplicate subsamples at a rate of at least 1 per
  10 samples to assess preparation variability. Analytical duplicates
  should agree within 5% RPD for C and N concentrations.
- Include a laboratory reference material (e.g., NIST SRM 1515
  Apple Leaves or NIST SRM 1547 Peach Leaves) in each analytical
  batch to verify accuracy [@kalra1998].
- Document all cleaning steps in the laboratory notebook, especially
  the blank grind between samples when trace metal analysis is planned.
- Confirm drying completeness by re-weighing a subset of samples after
  an additional 4 hours of drying.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Plant tissue waste            | Standard trash (non-hazardous)           |
| Ethanol cleaning rinses       | Evaporate in fume hood or flammable waste |
| Used tin capsules (unfired)   | Standard trash                           |
| Quartz sand (blank grind)     | Standard trash                           |

## Training Record

Before processing plant tissue independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate safe Wiley mill operation (startup, feeding, cleaning,
   shutdown) under supervision
4. Process at least five samples under supervision, including
   decontamination steps between samples
5. If preparing samples for IRMS, demonstrate fine grinding and
   accurate weighing into tin capsules (target mass 3--5 mg, recorded
   to 0.001 mg)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
